items.q: So I told Earl then... And I was the musical director, so Earl -- we started to writing letters... and we started to book the band

ctx.x: Quinn Wilson was on bass. So you know as I told you, Earl and Ed Fox was having a feud at that time so --

items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: when I had joined Earl HInes later

ctx.x: later. I hadn't seen Booker in a long time. In fact, when I had joined Earl HInes later -- I'll get back to my story, but I have to say this in order to clarify some points that Mr. (Hinton) has asked me.

I was in Tuskegee, and of course his mother had then, after she had lost her husband, and that (inaudible) and she had gone back to Tuskegee where -- which her father founded, and she was teaching music there, and I happened to be there with Earl Fatha Hines, and I think this was around 1937, and she had told me that she don't hear from her son very much, and she heard he was very ill, and whatnot, and of course I was concerned, because Booker and I were raised together.

So later on, very late, very, very, very later, Booker came back to the United States, and he brought his wife and daughter with him, and his daughter's a very, very, very great, great, great singer, and artist, and in Rio de Janeiro, and when I was down there I saw her, but anyway, they came in and I signed the papers. (He) had been on the Jack Paar show, and then Booker, of course, got in touch with me, and I signed for her to stay in this country where I would be responsible for her while she was here.

items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: with Hines Heines I wrote many, many, many things.

ctx.x: And of course I used to write for the different groups and rock groups and everything, for Decca and RCA, and with Hines Heines I wrote many, many, many things. Jerome things, I did Summertime and all of that, I was the staff arranger, you know. And Sarah Vaughn, at one time she came into town and somebody was supposed to make the arrangements for a record date for her and they didn't even show up with the music. So she called me. At that time I had an office downtown, I was in 1650 Broadway, and sharing an office
